tasks.title: Setup HVM3 Baseline Environment
tasks.description: Clone HVM3 repo, build it, and verify examples run for baseline comparison.
tasks.details: Clone HVM3 from GitHub into 'hvm3' subfolder. Install GHC and Cabal if needed (macOS: 'brew install ghc cabal-install'). Build HVM3: 'cd hvm3 && cabal build'. Run sample: 'cabal run hvm -- run examples/bench_count.hvm -C -s' to generate baseline. Extract IC.md and INTERS.md for reference.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify HVM3 runs successfully and produces output. Check that examples/ directory contains .hvm files. Confirm IC.md and INTERS.md exist.

subtasks.title: Clone HVM3 Repository
subtasks.description: Clone the HVM3 repository from GitHub into a subfolder named 'hvm3'.
subtasks.details: Execute 'git clone https://github.com/HigherOrderCO/HVM3.git hvm3' in the project root. Verify the clone succeeded and examples directory exists.
subtasks.testStrategy: Check that hvm3/ directory exists and contains examples/*.hvm files.

subtasks.title: Install Haskell Toolchain (macOS)
subtasks.description: Install GHC and Cabal for building HVM3 on macOS.
subtasks.details: Run 'brew install ghc cabal-install' to install Haskell toolchain. Verify installation with 'ghc --version' and 'cabal --version'.
subtasks.testStrategy: Confirm ghc and cabal commands are available and output version numbers.

subtasks.title: Build HVM3
subtasks.description: Build HVM3 using Cabal to generate the baseline runtime.
subtasks.details: Navigate to hvm3/ and run 'cabal update && cabal build'. Ensure build completes without errors.
subtasks.testStrategy: Build succeeds and 'cabal run hvm -- --help' shows usage information.

subtasks.title: Verify HVM3 Examples Run
subtasks.description: Run sample HVM3 examples to establish baselines for comparison.
subtasks.details: Run 'cabal run hvm -- run examples/bench_count.hvm -C -s' from hvm3/ directory. Capture output for baseline comparison. Test 2-3 other examples.
subtasks.testStrategy: Examples run successfully and produce normalized output plus MIPS statistics.

subtasks.title: Extract Reference Documentation
subtasks.description: Locate and extract IC.md and INTERS.md from HVM3 repo for implementation reference.
subtasks.details: Find IC.md and INTERS.md in hvm3/ (likely in docs/ or root). Copy or symlink to project root for easy reference. Read both to understand term grammar and interaction rules.
subtasks.testStrategy: Confirm both files are accessible and contain IC grammar and interaction rule specifications.

tasks.title: Setup Development Environment
tasks.description: Install Gforth (macOS) and create the initial project scaffold with modular Forth files.
tasks.details: Install Gforth using 'brew install gforth' (macOS). Create src/ directory with files: fvm.fs (main include), core.fs (primitives like tags, ALLOC), parse.fs (parser), heap.fs (heap management), reduce.fs (WHNF), interact.fs (interaction rules), collapse.fs (normalization), book.fs (book loading), cli.fs (CLI), errors.fs (error handling). Use Gforth's include mechanism for modularity. Ensure portability with ANSI Forth where possible.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify Gforth installation by running 'gforth --version'. Test scaffold by including fvm.fs and checking for no errors.

subtasks.title: Install Gforth Interpreter (macOS)
subtasks.description: Install the Gforth Forth interpreter on macOS to enable development and execution of Forth code.
subtasks.details: Use Homebrew: 'brew install gforth'. Ensure the installation completes without errors and verify the version to confirm compatibility with ANSI Forth standards.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run 'gforth --version' in the terminal and check that it outputs the version number without errors.

subtasks.title: Create Project Directory Structure
subtasks.description: Set up the initial directory for the project to organize all Forth source files and related assets.
subtasks.details: Create 'src/' subdirectory in the project root for Forth source files. Create 'examples/' symlink to hvm3/examples for test data. Create 'tests/' directory for test scripts.
subtasks.testStrategy: Navigate to src/ and confirm directory exists. Verify examples/ symlink points to hvm3/examples/.

subtasks.title: Create Main Include File (fvm.fs)
subtasks.description: Develop the main include file that serves as the entry point for including all other modular Forth files.
subtasks.details: In src/, create 'fvm.fs' as the primary file that uses Gforth's include mechanism to load other modules. Include directives like 'include core.fs', 'include errors.fs', 'include parse.fs', etc., to ensure modularity and portability with ANSI Forth.
subtasks.testStrategy: Attempt to include 'fvm.fs' in a Gforth session and check for any syntax errors or missing file errors, ensuring all includes are correctly referenced.

subtasks.title: Create Stub Files for All Modules
subtasks.description: Create empty/stub Forth files for all modules to ensure clean includes.
subtasks.details: Create stub files in src/: core.fs, errors.fs, heap.fs, parse.fs, reduce.fs, interact.fs, collapse.fs, book.fs, cli.fs. Each should have a comment header describing its purpose and a simple test word (e.g., ': TEST-CORE ." Core loaded" CR ;').
subtasks.testStrategy: Load 'fvm.fs' in Gforth and execute test words from each module to confirm all files load without errors.

tasks.title: Implement Error Handling Infrastructure
tasks.description: Create error handling system for parse errors, runtime errors, and debugging.
tasks.details: In errors.fs, implement error reporting words: PARSE-ERROR, RUNTIME-ERROR, AFFINE-ERROR. Add stack trace capability and graceful error messages. Implement DEBUG? flag for verbose output. Add utility words for assertions and validation.
tasks.testStrategy: Test error reporting with intentional errors. Verify error messages are clear and include context (line numbers, token info).

subtasks.title: Implement Basic Error Words
subtasks.description: Create fundamental error reporting words for different error types.
subtasks.details: Define PARSE-ERROR, RUNTIME-ERROR, AFFINE-ERROR words in errors.fs. Each should accept a string message and print formatted error with context. Include file/line info if available.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test each error word manually to verify output format and program termination behavior.

subtasks.title: Add Debug and Trace Utilities
subtasks.description: Implement debugging flags and trace output for development.
subtasks.details: Add DEBUG? variable for verbose mode. Implement TRACE word for printing execution steps. Add ASSERT word for runtime validation. Create .TERM word for pretty-printing terms during debug.
subtasks.testStrategy: Toggle DEBUG? and verify trace output appears/disappears. Test ASSERT with true/false conditions.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Break down into subtasks for defining primitives, implementing heap allocation, and adding garbage collection.

tasks.title: Implement Core Primitives and Heap Management
tasks.description: Define core primitives including tags, labs, and heap allocation with simple GC.
tasks.details: In core.fs, define constants for all IC tags from IC.md (LAM, APP, SUP, DUP, VAR, ERA, CTR, U32, etc.). Implement term packing/unpacking words for Forth CELL size. In heap.fs, implement ALLOC word for circular buffer heap (4k-16k cells). Add simple mark-sweep GC: traverse stack for roots, mark reachable, sweep free. Start with manual GC trigger, add automatic later.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test ALLOC by allocating and freeing cells, checking heap size. Test GC by forcing allocation until trigger, verify no leaks via heap stability. Test term pack/unpack roundtrip.

subtasks.title: Define IC Term Tags and Constants
subtasks.description: Define constants for all term tags from IC.md in core.fs.
subtasks.details: Based on IC.md from HVM3, define all tag constants: TAG-LAM, TAG-APP, TAG-SUP, TAG-DUP, TAG-VAR, TAG-ERA, TAG-CTR, TAG-U32, TAG-OP2, TAG-REF. Use sequential numbering starting from 0.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify all tag constants are defined and have unique values. Print values to confirm.

subtasks.title: Implement Term Packing/Unpacking
subtasks.description: Create words to pack/unpack terms into Forth cells (tag:5b, lab:18b, val:40b or adapted to CELL size).
subtasks.details: Define PACK-TERM ( tag lab val -- cell ) and UNPACK-TERM ( cell -- tag lab val ). Adapt bit layout to Forth's CELL size (32 or 64 bit). Add utility words: GET-TAG, GET-LAB, GET-VAL, SET-TAG, SET-LAB, SET-VAL.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test roundtrip: pack then unpack should return original values. Test edge cases (max values for each field).

subtasks.title: Implement Basic Heap Allocation
subtasks.description: Create heap buffer and ALLOC word for term storage.
subtasks.details: In heap.fs, CREATE HEAP 16384 CELLS ALLOT for 16k cell buffer. Implement HEAP-PTR variable for current allocation pointer. Define ALLOC ( n -- addr ) to allocate n cells and return address. Implement circular wraparound.
subtasks.testStrategy: Allocate various sizes, verify addresses are valid and within HEAP bounds. Test wraparound at buffer end.

subtasks.title: Implement Mark-Sweep Garbage Collection
subtasks.description: Add GC with mark phase (traverse from roots) and sweep phase (free unmarked cells).
subtasks.details: Create MARK-TABLE for tracking marked cells. Implement MARK-FROM-ROOT ( addr -- ) to recursively mark reachable terms. Implement SWEEP to free unmarked cells. Add GC-COLLECT word to trigger collection. Start with manual trigger.
subtasks.testStrategy: Create terms, mark some as roots, run GC, verify unmarked terms are freed. Check heap stability after multiple GC cycles.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Split into subtasks for creating the mapping structure and implementing substitution logic with affine checks.

tasks.title: Implement Substitution Map
tasks.description: Create a substitution map for variable binding and resolution with affine tracking.
tasks.details: In core.fs or new subst.fs, CREATE SUBST 1024 CELLS ALLOT for name->loc mapping. Implement hash-based lookup for efficiency. Add SUBST-PUT ( name loc -- ) and SUBST-GET ( name -- loc|0 ). Implement affine variable tracking: SUBST-USE ( name -- ) increments use count, error if >1. Add SUBST-CLEAR for scope cleanup.
tasks.testStrategy: Test with simple terms: parse 'λx.x', substitute x, verify correct loc. Check affine violations by attempting dup-use and assert error. Test hash collisions.

subtasks.title: Create Substitution Data Structure
subtasks.description: Set up hash-based substitution map for variable name-to-location mappings.
subtasks.details: In subst.fs, CREATE SUBST 1024 CELLS ALLOT. Implement simple hash function for names. Structure: each entry is ( hash name-addr loc use-count ). Implement SUBST-HASH ( name-addr -- index ) for hashing.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test hash function distributes names reasonably. Verify SUBST table is accessible.

subtasks.title: Implement Substitution Operations
subtasks.description: Create SUBST-PUT, SUBST-GET, and SUBST-USE words for managing substitutions.
subtasks.details: Implement SUBST-PUT ( name-addr loc -- ) to store binding. Implement SUBST-GET ( name-addr -- loc|0 ) to retrieve binding. Implement SUBST-USE ( name-addr -- ) to track usage and enforce affine property (error if use-count > 1). Add SUBST-CLEAR to reset table.
subtasks.testStrategy: Store bindings, retrieve them, verify correctness. Test affine enforcement: use variable twice should error. Test CLEAR resets table.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Divide into subtasks for tokenization, parsing each term type (LAM, APP, etc.), handling global vars, and outputting to dict.

tasks.title: Build Parser for IC Grammar (Minimal Subset First)
tasks.description: Implement recursive descent parser for HVM files, starting with LAM, APP, VAR subset.
tasks.details: In parse.fs, implement tokenizer using Gforth's WORD or custom. Define PARSE-TERM as dispatcher. Start with minimal subset: PARSE-LAM (λx.body), PARSE-APP (@f x), PARSE-VAR (variable refs). Add error handling for malformed input. Output terms as heap-allocated structures. Defer full grammar (SUP, DUP, CTR, etc.) to later subtask.
tasks.testStrategy: Parse simple HVM files: 'λx.x', '(@(λx.x) y)'. Verify term structure in heap. Test error handling with invalid syntax. Compare parsed AST structure with HVM3.

subtasks.title: Implement Tokenizer
subtasks.description: Create tokenization system for reading HVM source.
subtasks.details:
In parse.fs, implement NEXT-TOKEN ( -- addr len ) to read next token from input. Handle whitespace, comments, special chars (λ @ ( ) { }). Use Gforth's WORD or implement custom tokenizer with lookahead. Store current file/line for error reporting.
<info added on 2025-11-11T00:06:08.651Z>
Tokenizer fully implemented with all IC token types. 4 tokenizer tests passing. Location: parse.fs:90-227.
</info added on 2025-11-11T00:06:08.651Z>
subtasks.testStrategy: Feed test strings, verify tokens are correctly extracted including special characters and whitespace handling.

subtasks.title: Parse Lambda Terms (LAM)
subtasks.description: Implement PARSE-LAM for lambda abstractions. [Updated: 11/10/2025]
subtasks.details:
Define PARSE-LAM to parse 'λx.body' syntax. Extract variable name, bind in SUBST, parse body recursively, create LAM term in heap with binding to body. Handle nested lambdas.
<info added on 2025-11-11T00:06:13.627Z>
PARSE-LAM implemented. Fixed stack manipulation bug (use 2 PICK). Location: parse.fs:247-286.
</info added on 2025-11-11T00:06:13.627Z>
subtasks.testStrategy: Parse 'λx.x', verify creates LAM term with correct variable binding. Test nested 'λx.λy.x'.

subtasks.title: Parse Application Terms (APP)
subtasks.description: Implement PARSE-APP for function application.
subtasks.details: Define PARSE-APP to parse '(@f x)' or '(f x)' syntax. Parse function and argument recursively, create APP term in heap linking to both. Handle multiple arguments as nested applications.
subtasks.testStrategy: Parse '(@(λx.x) y)', verify creates APP with LAM and VAR children. Test multi-argument applications.

subtasks.title: Parse Variable References (VAR)
subtasks.description: Implement PARSE-VAR for variable lookups.
subtasks.details: Define PARSE-VAR to handle identifier tokens. Look up in SUBST map, create VAR term pointing to binding location. Error if unbound variable (unless forward ref allowed).
subtasks.testStrategy: Parse 'λx.x', verify inner 'x' resolves to lambda binding. Test unbound variable errors.

subtasks.title: Add Error Recovery and Reporting
subtasks.description: Integrate error handling into parser with helpful messages.
subtasks.details: Wrap parse functions with error checking. Report file:line:column for errors. Give helpful messages like 'Expected λ or @ but got X'. Test with intentionally malformed input.
subtasks.testStrategy: Parse invalid syntax, verify error messages are clear and include location information.

subtasks.title: Extend Parser for Full IC Grammar
subtasks.description: Add support for SUP, DUP, ERA, CTR, U32, OP2 from IC.md.
subtasks.details:
Add PARSE-SUP (superposition), PARSE-DUP (duplication), PARSE-ERA (erasure), PARSE-CTR (constructors), PARSE-U32 (numbers), PARSE-OP2 (binary ops). Reference IC.md for exact syntax. Update PARSE-TERM dispatcher.
<info added on 2025-11-11T00:06:19.328Z>
Extended with ERA/SUP/DUP parsers. 10/10 tests passing. 80% complete. TODO: label numbers, top-level defs. parse.fs:317-497.
</info added on 2025-11-11T00:06:19.328Z>
subtasks.testStrategy: Parse examples using each construct. Verify term structures match HVM3. Test complex nested combinations.

tasks.expansionPrompt: Separate into subtasks for loading and parsing books, and implementing global linking.

tasks.title: Implement Book Loading and Global Linking
tasks.description: Load parsed books into Forth dict with function definitions and linking.
tasks.details: In book.fs, implement LOAD-BOOK ( filename -- ) to parse HVM file with multiple definitions. Store functions in dictionary with name, arity, and term pointer. Implement function lookup: FIND-FUN ( name -- term-addr|0 ). Handle forward references with two-pass: first collect definitions, then resolve refs. Support HVM's '@name' reference syntax.
tasks.testStrategy: Load HVM file with multiple functions. Verify dict entries correct. Test function calls resolve to definitions. Test forward references.

subtasks.title: Implement Function Dictionary
subtasks.description: Create dictionary structure for storing parsed function definitions.
subtasks.details: In book.fs, CREATE BOOK-DICT 256 CELLS ALLOT for function storage. Each entry: ( name-addr arity term-addr ). Implement BOOK-PUT ( name arity term -- ) and BOOK-FIND ( name -- arity term | 0 0 ).
subtasks.testStrategy: Store functions, retrieve them, verify all fields correct. Test name collision handling.

subtasks.title: Implement Two-Pass Loading
subtasks.description: Parse file in two passes: collect definitions, then resolve references.
subtasks.details: First pass: PARSE-DEF parses 'name = term' and stores in BOOK-DICT with term containing unresolved refs. Second pass: LINK-REFS traverses terms, replaces '@name' refs with term pointers using BOOK-FIND. Handle circular references.
subtasks.testStrategy: Load file with forward refs. Verify second pass resolves all refs. Test mutual recursion.

subtasks.title: Implement LOAD-BOOK Entry Point
subtasks.description: Create main interface for loading HVM book files.
subtasks.details: Define LOAD-BOOK ( filename-addr len -- ) to open file, parse all definitions, link refs. Integrate with error handling for file not found, parse errors, unresolved refs. Set 'main' as entry point if present.
subtasks.testStrategy: Load HVM3 example files. Verify all functions parsed and linked. Test error cases (missing file, undefined refs).

tasks.expansionPrompt: Break into subtasks for defining WHNF loop, implementing IS-VALUE? checks, and adding interpreted mode.

tasks.title: Implement Reducer and WHNF Loop
tasks.description: Build the WHNF (Weak Head Normal Form) reducer loop for term evaluation with pattern matching support.
tasks.details: In reduce.fs, define WHNF ( term -- whnf-term ) as main reduction loop. Implement IS-VALUE? ( term -- flag ) to check for LAM/SUP/CTR/MATCH (values that don't reduce further). Loop: repeatedly apply one interaction step until value or stuck. Implement INTERACT-STEP ( term -- term' ) that dispatches to appropriate interaction rule including MATCH-REDUCE. Add iteration counter for stats. Pattern matching (~n { 0: ..., 1+p: ... }) fully implemented with numeric case selection and variable binding.
tasks.testStrategy: Test WHNF on simple terms: '(@(λx.x) y)' should reduce to 'y'. Verify loop terminates on values. Test stuck terms (unresolved refs). Count interactions. Test pattern matching: ~n { 0: 42, 1+p: p } applied to 0 returns 42.

subtasks.title: Implement IS-VALUE? Predicate
subtasks.description: Create predicate to check if term is in weak head normal form.
subtasks.details: In reduce.fs, define IS-VALUE? ( term -- flag ) that checks term tag. Return TRUE for LAM, SUP, CTR, MATCH (constructors/values). Return FALSE for APP, DUP (redexes that need reduction). Handle all IC tags appropriately.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test with various term types. LAM/SUP/CTR/MATCH should return TRUE, APP/DUP FALSE. Verify covers all IC tags.

subtasks.title: Implement INTERACT-STEP Dispatcher
subtasks.description: Create dispatcher that applies one interaction step based on term structure.
subtasks.details: Define INTERACT-STEP ( term -- term' ) that examines term tag and dispatches to specific interaction rules. Handles APP (APP-LAM, APP-ERA, APP-SUP), DUP (DUP-ERA, DUP-LAM, DUP-SUP), OP2, MATCH, REF cases. Increment global ITR-COUNT counter. Includes debug tracing.
subtasks.testStrategy: Call INTERACT-STEP on terms, verify counter increments. Verify dispatcher correctly routes to all implemented rules without crashing.

subtasks.title: Implement WHNF Reduction Loop
subtasks.description: Create main reduction loop that reduces term to weak head normal form.
subtasks.details: Define WHNF ( term -- whnf-term ) as: BEGIN DUP IS-VALUE? 0= WHILE INTERACT-STEP REPEAT. Handles stuck terms gracefully. Iteration counter for stats. Integrated with MATCH-REDUCE for pattern matching support.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test with identity function applied to value (should terminate). Test with pure value (should return immediately). Test pattern matching reduction: ~n { 0: 42 } applied to 0 terminates correctly.

subtasks.title: Implement Pattern Matching Reduction
subtasks.description: Add MATCH-REDUCE rule for numeric pattern matching (~n { 0: ..., 1+p: ... }).
subtasks.details: Implement MATCH-REDUCE ( match-term -- result-or-0 ) that extracts scrutinee, checks U32 type, selects zero/successor branch, binds successor variable (p = n-1), evaluates selected body via WHNF, cleans up bindings. Handles numeric patterns (lab=0). Constructor patterns (lab=1) stubbed for future.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test zero case: ~n { 0: 42, 1+p: p } applied to 0 returns 42. Test successor case: applied to 1 binds p=0 and evaluates successor body. Verify affine binding cleanup.

subtasks.title: Implement Normalization Functions
subtasks.description: Add recursive NORMALIZE and helper functions for deep reduction.
subtasks.details: Implement NORMALIZE ( term -- norm-term ) that reduces to WHNF then recursively normalizes subterms. Add NORMALIZE-LAM, NORMALIZE-SUP, NORMALIZE-MATCH, NORMALIZE-APP, NORMALIZE-DUP, NORMALIZE-CTR, NORMALIZE-OP2. Use RECURSE for mutual recursion. Handle all term types.
subtasks.testStrategy: Test deep normalization on nested terms. Verify all subterms reduced. Test pattern matching normalization preserves structure.

master.expansionPrompt: Create subtasks for each major interaction rule (e.g., APP-LAM, DUP-SUP) and adding compiled mode fast-paths.

master.title: Implement Core Interaction Rules
master.description: Implement 8 core interaction rules from INTERS.md as Forth words in interact.fs.
master.details: All 8 core interaction rules are fully implemented in src/interact.fs using the DEFER/IS pattern: APP-LAM (line 115), APP-SUP (line 346), DUP-ERA (line 126), DUP-LAM (line 268), DUP-SUP (line 215), CTR-DUP (line 428), OP2-U32 (line 366), and MATCH-REDUCE (line 614). Pattern matching (numeric + constructor) is fully functional. Code compiles successfully. However, runtime bugs prevent tests from passing: 1) Duplicate NORMALIZE in collapse.fs overwrites reduce.fs version, 2) APP-SUP/OP2-COMPUTE naming conflict, 3) Missing SUBST-CLEAR between files, 4) NORMALIZE-OP2 stack corruption, 5) Incomplete SUBST-WALK. Estimated 1.5 hours to fix all runtime issues. Each rule checks if pattern matches, applies rewrite, returns new term. Integrated with INTERACT-STEP dispatcher from Task 7. Reference INTERS.md for exact semantics. Start with interpreted mode (no optimization).
master.testStrategy: Unit test each rule individually with hand-crafted terms. Verify output matches expected rewrite. Test with HVM3 examples like bench_count.hvm. Compare reduction traces. After fixing runtime bugs, re-run tests to ensure all pass.

subtasks.title: Implement APP-LAM (Beta Reduction)
subtasks.description: Core beta reduction rule: (@(λx.body) arg) -> body[x:=arg].
subtasks.details:
In interact.fs, define APP-LAM ( app-term -- reduced-term ). Check term is APP with LAM function. Extract lambda var, body, and argument. Substitute arg for var in body using SUBST mechanism. Return substituted body.
